column1: What is IAM's policy evaluation order?
column2: Implicit deny (default) → explicit Allow lifts it → explicit Deny overrides everything. One explicit Deny anywhere = denied. Order, count, and specificity do NOT matter.

column1: Which AWS region does IAM live in?
column2: None — IAM is a global service. No region selection. (API endpoint historically runs from us-east-1, but conceptually global.)

column1: What's the credential difference between an IAM User and an IAM Role?
column2:
User: long-lived credentials (password, access key) that persist until rotated.
Role: no permanent credentials; on assume, AWS STS issues temporary credentials that auto-expire (default 1h, max 12h).

column1: What two policies does an IAM Role need to be useful?
column2:
1) Trust policy (assume_role_policy on aws_iam_role) — WHO can assume me.
2) Permissions policy (attached separately) — WHAT I can do once assumed.
Either half missing = role is broken.

column1: Why doesn't EC2 attach to an IAM Role directly?
column2: EC2 attaches to an Instance Profile, a thin wrapper around a role. Console hides this; Terraform requires aws_iam_instance_profile explicitly and a reference from aws_instance.iam_instance_profile. Lambda, ECS, etc. take roles directly — EC2 is the special case.

column1: In Terraform IAM cross-references, when do you use .name vs .arn?
column2:
.name for principals (users, groups, roles) in management API calls — they only exist within your account, so name is unambiguous.
.arn for policies — they may live in the aws account namespace (managed) or your account, so ARN with account ID disambiguates.
Plan and validate do NOT catch mistakes here.

column1: What's the difference between aws_iam_user_group_membership and aws_iam_group_membership?
column2:
aws_iam_user_group_membership: user-side, additive ("put this user in these groups"). Safe.
aws_iam_group_membership: group-side, exclusive ("these are the ONLY members"). Removes anyone not listed on next apply. Dangerous.

column1: What does the prefix-less aws_iam_policy_attachment do, and why avoid it?
column2: Manages ALL attachments of one specific policy across users/groups/roles. If anyone attaches that same policy anywhere else (manually, or in another config), Terraform removes it on next apply. Use the principal-prefixed aws_iam_{user,group,role}_policy_attachment instead.

column1: In HCL, what's the difference between aws_iam_group.developers and "aws_iam_group.developers"?
column2:
Without quotes: a reference expression, evaluated by Terraform to a resource (then dot into .name / .arn / .id).
With quotes: a literal string of 23 characters, passed through unchanged. Most common HCL beginner bug.

column1: What do +, -, ~, and -/+ mean in terraform plan output?
column2: + create. - destroy. ~ in-place update (attribute changed, resource not recreated). -/+ destroy and recreate (an attribute marked ForceNew changed; plan shows "# forces replacement" next to it).

column1: Does changing the name on aws_iam_user force destroy and recreate?
column2:
NO — aws_iam_user.name is in-place updatable (provider calls AWS UpdateUser with NewUserName).
BUT aws_iam_policy.name IS ForceNew (destroys and recreates, because the ARN embeds the name). Different IAM resources behave differently; always read the plan.

column1: What is the IAM policy Version field (e.g. "2012-10-17")?
column2: The IAM policy LANGUAGE version (policy schema). Always "2012-10-17" for modern IAM policies — NOT a free-form version field. The aws_iam_policy_document data source adds it automatically.
